chunks: And We removed whatever was in their breasts of rancour; streams of running water flow beneath them. They say: 'All praise is due to Allah, who guided us to this; and we would not have been guided if Allah had not guided us. The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth.' And they are called: 'This is Paradise, which you have inherited for what you used to do.'

key_terms.أُورِثْتُمُوهَا: You have been made to inherit it
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: All praise is due to Allah
key_terms.غِلٍّ: Rancour or hatred in the chest/heart

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the inhabitants of Paradise regarding their hearts and their gratitude according to Surah Al-A'raf?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia exegesis to illustrate the purification of the heart (tazkiyah) in the afterlife, describes the complete eradication of 'ghill' (inner malice or envy) among the inhabitants of Paradise. It underscores the theological principle that while human deeds are the mechanism of reward, divine guidance (hidayah) is the ultimate cause, as affirmed by the phrase 'Hadana Allah'. The mention of flowing rivers beneath them signifies the eternal, tangible bliss that complements their spiritual purity.
